notes: larazon.pe is WordPress + Yoast. Probes (all via polite_fetch): /robots.txt 200 and permissive (only /wp-admin, /wp-includes, /?s=, /refer/, /xmlrpc.php etc. disallowed) and it advertises https://larazon.pe/sitemap_index.xml. /sitemap.xml 403 (the earlier failure: that file does not exist; only sitemap_index.xml does). /wp-json/wp/v2/posts 401 (REST disabled for anonymous). /feed/ 200 but it serves the HTML homepage (248 KB), not a feed. /wp-sitemap.xml 200, same content as sitemap_index.xml. Wayback CDX was already reported timing out by the previous attempt. ROUTE THAT WORKS: sitemap_index.xml (2 requests total) is a Yoast sitemapindex with 159 children: numbered post sitemaps post-sitemap.xml..post-sitemap101.xml plus page/category/post_tag/edicion_impresa sitemaps. post-sitemap.xml (the bare one) is the OLDEST file here (entries 2017-11-24 onward, plus junk like /blog/), while the newest content sits in the highest number: post-sitemap101.xml holds 796 posts from 2026-09-18 to 2026-10-26, i.e. the whole 31-day window in one file. The script fetches the index, keeps numbered post sitemaps whose index lastmod is not older than the window start, then reads <loc>/<lastmod> pairs and takes the lastmod date-part. Result: 656 unique URLs, 31/31 days (09-30=28, 10-10=23, 10-20=24; min 2 on Sunday 10-04, weekends are genuinely thin). Dates verified: 17 of 18 re-fetched articles have JSON-LD datePublished exactly equal to the sitemap lastmod date, 1 drifted +1 day (lastmod is the post_modified time on edited posts), so max observed drift is 1 day, inside the check tolerance. All 18 re-fetched samples returned 200 with 3.7k-10.9k chars of article text; the 30 /portada-diario-la-razon-* print-front-page posts yield ~3.0k chars, still above 1500. No low_volume needed.
